items.basis: The claimed mechanism contradicts fundamental PEMFC water management principles; absence of nitrogen in pure oxygen systems reduces the driving force for water back-diffusion from cathode to anode, which would exacerbate membrane dehydration rather than reduce it, as evidenced by [doi:10.1016/s1452-3981(23)12855-0]

Maintaining stack temperature at 80°C while varying separator temperature creates thermal gradients that would induce mechanical stress on the membrane and bipolar plates, leading to premature failure, violating the boundary condition of stable operation at high current density

The candidate's own evidence [doi:10.13374/j.issn2095-9389.2021.04.30.002] demonstrates that membrane humidification efficiency is highly dependent on temperature differentials, contradicting the claim that varying separator temperature alone can reduce dehydration without addressing humidification method

The proposed intervention fails to address the root cause of membrane dehydration at high current density, which is the electro-osmotic drag overwhelming back-diffusion, making it equivalent to the baseline status quo in performance-critical scenarios

The system cannot simultaneously maintain stack temperature at 80°C while varying separator temperature without complex thermal management that would increase parasitic load beyond the 10% boundary condition, as shown in [doi:10.3390/biomimetics11080545]

The prediction fails to define how "membrane dehydration" is measured, whether it's through resistance changes, water content, or voltage fluctuations, making the testable prediction unscientifically verifiable as noted in [doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-7081268/v1]
